newsitem.title: ITALY: Early turnout low in Italy's local elections.
newsitem.headline: Early turnout low in Italy's local elections.

text.p: Early turnout figures from local elections in more than 1,100 towns and cities in Italy on Sunday suggested many voters were staying away from polling stations.
The figures, including from the big northern cities of Milan, Turin and Trieste, showed turnout was well down compared with the previous municipal polls in 1993.
Polling stations opened at 7 a.m. (0500 GMT) and close at 10 p.m. (2000 GMT).
In Milan, the highest profile election in the contests for mayor and local councils, turnout was 7.4 percent at 11 a.m. (0900 GMT), down from 9.6 percent at the same stage in 1993.

In Turin, nine percent of the eligible electorate had voted compared with 15 percent four years ago, while in Trieste turnout was down three percentage points at 12.4 percent, according to election officials.
Friday was a national holiday in Italy. Many Italians have left their homes for long weekends away, influencing early turnout.
Almost all the key mayoral races in big cities and larger towns are expected to go to a second round run-off on May 11 between the two top contenders.
